clue.text: Article that's penned about a cardinal?

indicators.note: what is penned is shut inside a pen, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: the definite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written about a senior churchman of the Roman Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but the question mark points to cardinal numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, and three is one example of them.

clue.text: Following well behind, runs out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shadowing someone at a distance, as a detective does

explanation.surface: A runner trailing far back in a race who then gives up and drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail is to follow covertly, and also to diminish gradually until it fades; both senses share this verb form.

clue.text: Two overweight people making a dessert

parts.note: a roly-poly is a plump person
pudding is a jokey term for a fat or stodgy person

explanation.surface: A pair of portly diners together cooking up something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both halves: each of the two overweight people is a different informal word for a plump person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly pudding is a traditional British steamed or baked suet pudding rolled with jam.

clue.text: Comic — 'Eagle' brought round I learned

indicators.note: brought round means placed around something, so the bird encloses the next piece

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
taken as written
learned and wise both mean knowledgeable

explanation.surface: A comic-strip magazine helped teach me to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eagle' was a famous British boys' comic, which makes 'Comic' look like a description of it. Ernie Wise was the straight man of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was a British comedian, and a comic is another word for a comedian.

clue.text: Cook does stunning salad dish incorporating right mayonnaise sauce

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of the phrase before it
to cook something is to work it over, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the bulk of the letters to rearrange
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the cook produces a striking salad dish with the correct mayonnaise-based sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a person in the kitchen, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousand Island dressing is a salad dressing made from mayonnaise with ketchup and chopped relish.

clue.text: Daughter, breaking obligations, drifts

definitions.note: a noun here: drifts and tides are both currents

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one letter enters the word that follows

parts.note: ties are bonds or obligations
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter shirks her responsibilities and drifts through life.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifts are movements of water carried along, which is what tides are, as a plural noun.

clue.text: Completed approach in a very high gear

parts.note: over means finished
a drive is the approach road to a house

explanation.surface: A driver finishes the run-up to something in top gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' looks like a verb but is the noun for the road leading up to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdrive is an extra gear in a vehicle set higher than the usual top gear, for economical cruising.

clue.text: American article supporting southern girl

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so the earlier pieces go below the later one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
US is short for American
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A US newspaper piece that backs a Southern girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is set by position in the column, not by the order of words in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, and setters use girl to clue such names.

clue.text: MPs mention NCO, so irrational — not in his right mind?

indicators.note: irrational means lacking order or reason, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament bring up a non-commissioned officer, who is accordingly unreasonable and perhaps mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Non compos mentis is Latin legal phrase for being of unsound mind, i.e. mentally incapable.

clue.text: See 4
Most important element

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the heavy metal with symbol Pb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase, the key element, but it splits into two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead as an adjective means chief or principal, and as a noun it is a chemical element, a heavy grey metal.

clue.text: Drafted in one male 'Fleet Street' editor?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male
Fleet Street in London was the home of the national newspapers, so it stands for the press
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A man brought in as editor of a national newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet Street' is a London street long synonymous with the British newspaper industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressment was the old practice of forcing men into naval service, so impressed means conscripted or drafted.

clue.text: Trap quickly springs back on tail of mouse

indicators.note: springing back means recoiling the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: soon means quickly or shortly

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of mouse

explanation.surface: A mousetrap snaps shut on the creature's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that tightens, used as a snare to trap animals.

clue.text: Resentment shown by one I cut off back in Turkish port

parts.note: gall means bitterness or resentment
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back means returning the way it came, so the phrase before it is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone bitter after being amputated by a person, back home in a Turkish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli (Gelibolu) is a port on the Dardanelles in Turkey, famous for the First World War campaign.

clue.text: Class to be trained using hurdles

indicators.note: what is trained is drilled and shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A PE lesson in which pupils learn to jump hurdles.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes 'to be' as well as 'Class', with 'trained' alone the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurdles are barriers to be jumped, and figuratively any obstacles in one's way, so the two plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Thick sauce, when written about, is 'savoury'

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the words are written in the opposite direction

parts.note: a dip is a thick sauce for dunking
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A food writer describing a thick sauce as savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a rare word meaning having a strong, pleasant flavour, so it fits savoury or tasty.

clue.text: Put one's foot down on spring flower

parts.note: to put one's foot down is to accelerate, i.e. go fast
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Stamping on a flower that has sprung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but here it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Veronica, so it is one example of a flower.

clue.text: The sound of bluebottles in small wood

indicators.note: the sound of a word means we use how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: bluebottle is old British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform

explanation.surface: Buzzing flies heard among the trees of a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottles' suggests buzzing flies in a wood; it is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket or group of trees, so it is a little wood.

clue.text: Wimbledon champion — first to congratulate another, we hear

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of congratulate

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its spoken sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Arthur Ashe was another Wimbledon champion, 1975

explanation.surface: A tennis champion is the first to shake another winner's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another Wimbledon champion, Arthur Ashe, whose surname is pronounced like the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Cash, the Australian, won the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1987.

clue.text: 'Boy's Own' has no western writer

parts.note: Steven is a boy's name, with the possessive 's

indicators.note: has no means a letter is missing, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: The old boys' magazine Boy's Own Paper lacks a cowboy story by some author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy's Own' was a British magazine for boys, which disguises a boy's name plus 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped, so a writer.

clue.text: Lifelike, as is to be expected

definitions.meaning: first meaning: true to life, realistic

explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits two meanings of the same adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural describes something realistic in appearance and also what is normal or expected in the circumstances.

clue.text: Irish boy drinking drop of draught in saloon

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the name

parts.note: Sean is an Irish boy's name

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of draught

explanation.surface: An Irish lad sipping draught beer in the saloon bar of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' sets up a pub, but it is the British word for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon is the British term for a sedan car, a closed car with a separate boot.

clue.text: Hot in pleasant alcove

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one letter goes within the next word

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Somewhere warm in a cosy nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess in a wall, which is the same thing as an alcove.

clue.text: A repair, by workers on time for a change

parts.note: taken as written
a mend is a repair
workers are men, as in a workforce
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Workmen doing a repair on schedule, for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' looks like an idiom meaning unusually, but it hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration made to a text such as a law, so it is a change.

clue.text: Counts gems pop initially overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: pearls are gems

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of pop

explanation.surface: Someone tallies the jewellery but Dad is ignored at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counts' looks like a verb but is the plural of the noblemen's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a continental nobleman, the equivalent of a British earl, so counts are earls.

clue.text: One may be copied to several people in Ohio's capital, maybe

definitions.text: One may be copied to several people
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a document sent out to many recipients
second meaning, cryptic: the capital (first) letter of Ohio is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something duplicated and sent to many residents of Columbus, Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ohio's capital' wants to be Columbus; it is the capital letter of Ohio, which is round.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a printed notice sent to many people; and O is literally a round-shaped character of the alphabet.

clue.text: For example, President must avoid crowds in exits

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
P is the abbreviation for president
to press is to crowd round

explanation.surface: A head of state who should keep away from the crowds at the exits.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out, so egresses are exits; the word is the formal counterpart of ingress.

clue.text: Based in Ely, sold disinfectant

indicators.note: based in means located within, so the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A disinfectant made and sold in the cathedral city of Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysol is a brand of household disinfectant and cleaner, so a trade name for one.
